title: Simplify repository configuration: schema cleanup, repo+local config layering, onboard skill, validator
summary: Architecture analysis for the four-part proposal that lands as one coordinated feature (per HITL decision-2): collapse persist_dirs/persist_system_dirs into a single persist:, derive watch_files and checks, add a layered <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml + ~/.config/egg/repositories.yaml model with replace-by-default merge semantics, add an /onboard-repo skill, and ship a write-time validator (egg validate-config CLI + an mcp__egg__validate_repo_config MCP tool). The recommended approach centralizes load+merge in a new shared/egg_config/repos.py imported by both config/repo_config.py and sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py so all ~15 callers see the same merged view, hard-deprecates the legacy schema (decision-4), reserves a forward-compatible version: 1 + template: hook (decision-13 + feedback Q4), and ships Python (uv/pip), Node (npm/pnpm/yarn), and Go detection in v1 (decision-14) with a registered detector plug-in seam to slot in bazel/gradle later.

decisions_summary.decision-2: One coordinated feature, not sequenced PRs (selected: opt-2)
decisions_summary.decision-3: persist: classifies entries by leading slash (selected: opt-1)
decisions_summary.decision-4: Hard-deprecate legacy schema immediately, no migration tool (selected: opt-4)
decisions_summary.decision-5: Centralized merge loader in new shared/egg_config/repos.py (selected: opt-1)
decisions_summary.decision-6: Both new egg validate-config CLI subcommand AND extend the MCP tool (selected: opt-1)
decisions_summary.decision-8: On unwritable repo: print to stdout + offer to append to user file (selected: opt-1)
decisions_summary.decision-9: Replace by default, no extends keyword for now (selected: opt-1)
decisions_summary.decision-10: Loader auto-discovers <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml; silent skip if absent (selected: opt-1)
decisions_summary.decision-11: Two-tier validator: errors block, warnings advise (selected: opt-1)
decisions_summary.decision-12: No migration helper; hand-migrate via deprecation docs (selected: opt-2)
decisions_summary.decision-13: Schema versioning (version: 1) on both files (selected: opt-1)
decisions_summary.decision-14: Detect Python (uv/pip), Node (npm/pnpm/yarn), Go in v1 only (selected: opt-1)

feedback_summary.Q1_upgrade_friction: Hard cutover OK, no migration tool — matches decision-4.
feedback_summary.Q2_repos_to_migrate: Just the egg repo itself (egg/.egg/repositories.yaml is canonical migration).
feedback_summary.Q3_priority: All four pieces are required and ship together — don't drop any.
feedback_summary.Q4_template_hook: Yes — reserve a template: schema field for follow-up template-library work.
feedback_summary.Q5_extra_validations: Add: auth_mode: user without GITHUB_USER_TOKEN; persist of empty dir; curl/wget in private mode network-locked context. Keep all the issue's listed checks.
feedback_summary.Q6_skill_confirmation: Always require AskUserQuestion confirmation per detected build_command — no auto-write.
feedback_summary.Q7_non_makefile_checks: Unknown today; design detector for plug-in extensibility (bazel/gradle/multi-stage).

current_contents: contract-rules.md (91 lines, contract state machine rules)
repo_side_egg_dir.implication: Adding repositories.yaml here is consistent with .egg/ as repo-side egg config; we will also need .egg/schemas/repositories.schema.json so the existing schema-driven tooling pattern carries over.

callers.implication: Centralizing the merge in shared/egg_config/repos.py (decision-5) means we update _load_config() in config/repo_config.py + the read site in sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py; every other caller inherits the merged view for free.

current_architecture.schema_versioning_today: No version field on repositories.yaml. Other YAML/JSON in the repo: shared/check-fixers.yml carries version: "1" (legacy workflow); .github/dependabot.yml uses version: 2 (GitHub standard). No graceful-degradation pattern is precedented for repo config — new in this change.

in_scope: Schema simplification (collapse persist_dirs+persist_system_dirs → persist:; derive watch_files; derive checks; add version: 1 + template: reservation; HARD-deprecate legacy keys)
Layered loader: read <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml + ~/.config/egg/repositories.yaml; deep-merge dicts, replace lists; centralized in shared/egg_config/repos.py

/onboard-repo skill (skills/onboard-repo/SKILL.md) with Python (uv/pip), Node (npm/pnpm/yarn), Go detection; AskUserQuestion confirmation per detected build_command; fallback to stdout-print + append-to-user-file when repo is unwritable

Migrate egg/.egg/repositories.yaml itself as part of rollout (per feedback Q2)
Update config/repositories.yaml.example to the new schema
Update docs (docs/guides/) covering layered model + onboarding skill

extends: keyword for additive list merging (decision-9 = ship without)
Repo template library (python-uv/node-pnpm) — reserved as template: schema hook only (feedback Q4)

Auto-rewrite of existing user configs (hand-migrate per Q1)

shape.template: (reserved, opt-in string identifier; loader does not yet resolve, just validates that it is a string when present)

build_commands.watch_files: (optional; if omitted, derived from manifest catalog: pyproject.toml, uv.lock, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, go.mod, go.sum, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, requirements*.txt, Gemfile.lock — the loader populates the resolved list before manifest.json is written so docker-setup.py sees explicit watch files)
build_commands.persist: (unified list, classified at runtime: leading-slash → system absolute path; otherwise repo-relative)

shape.checks: (optional; if omitted, derived from Makefile lint/test targets and package.json scripts)

operator_scoped_keys_forbidden_here: docker_setup.* (operator-level extras only — repo-scoped extras live in repo file's extra_packages)

repo_settings.<owner>/<repo>: (any per-repo key from repo file; user values OVERRIDE repo file at the leaf)

new_user_file_layout.validator_errors_when_user_file_sets_rep: warning, not error (existing files may already be doing this; tightening to error is a follow-up)

merge_semantics.dict_merge: Deep merge; user file wins at the leaf (decision-9 baseline behavior).
merge_semantics.list_merge: Replace by default. No extends: keyword. checks, persist, watch_files, extra_packages.apt, extra_packages.dnf, extra_packages.packages, local_repos.paths all replace.
merge_semantics.operator_scoped_top_level: Comes EXCLUSIVELY from user file; repo-file entries here are dropped with a warning.
merge_semantics.auto_discovery: When the loader is invoked against a checkout (path inferred from local_repos.paths or the cwd at MCP invocation time), it looks for <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml. Missing file is not an error (silent skip per decision-10).

persist_classification_rule.leading_slash: Absolute path. Routed to persist_system_dirs at manifest-write time.
persist_classification_rule.no_leading_slash: Repo-relative path. Routed to persist_dirs at manifest-write time.
persist_classification_rule.validator_check: If a relative path begins with .. or contains symlinks escaping the repo root, error.
persist_classification_rule.internal_compatibility: The manifest.json written to /tmp/repo-deps/ continues to use the existing two-list shape (persist_dirs + persist_system_dirs). docker-setup.py is NOT changed; the host-side classifier produces the legacy manifest fields from the unified persist: list. This keeps the build-time consumer untouched and preserves the #2090 fail-loud guarantees.

watch_files_derivation.rule: If build_commands exists and watch_files is omitted, the loader populates the resolved watch list by intersecting the catalog with files actually present in the repo, plus any Makefile target referenced by build_commands.commands.
watch_files_derivation.explicit_override: Listing watch_files explicitly disables derivation (the explicit list is used verbatim).
watch_files_derivation.validator_check: Heuristic — if commands include 'pip install' / 'uv sync' / 'npm install' / 'go mod' and the corresponding manifest is NOT in resolved watch list, warn.

rules: If checks is absent, scan repo's Makefile for lint and test targets (after include resolution; tolerate phony targets).
If a package.json is present, also scan scripts.lint and scripts.test.
If exactly one of {Makefile, package.json scripts} provides a target, the resolved checks block is [{name: lint, command: make lint}, {name: test, command: make test}] (or npm equivalents).
If both provide targets, prefer Makefile and add a warning suggesting the user pin checks: explicitly.
checks_derivation.validator_check: If checks.command references a Makefile target that does not exist after include resolution, error (blocks load); if it references a target whose body is empty / phony, warn.

schema_versioning.field: version: 1 (top-level integer, required at config-write time, optional at load time with a warning if absent)
schema_versioning.graceful_degradation: Loader accepts version <= LOADER_MAX_SUPPORTED (1 today); on version > LOADER_MAX_SUPPORTED logs a warning and proceeds with best-effort parsing (do not error — the operator may be running an older egg against a newer-schema repo file).
schema_versioning.future_breaking_changes: Bump LOADER_MAX_SUPPORTED only when a hard incompatibility is introduced. The version: 0 / unversioned legacy file is rejected with a clear error pointing to the migration doc (per decision-4 hard cutover).

template_hook_reservation.v1_behavior: Validator allows the field; loader stores it on the merged dict but takes no action.
template_hook_reservation.rationale: Reserves the spelling so a follow-up template-library PR (out-of-scope here) can land without another schema migration (per feedback Q4).

components.name: shared/egg_config/repos.py (new module — central loader+merger)
responsibilities: Single import point for the merged repo+user view used by config/repo_config.py and sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py.
load_repo_file(repo_path: Path | None) -> RepoFileConfig — parses <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml; returns empty cfg if absent.
load_user_file() -> UserFileConfig — parses ~/.config/egg/repositories.yaml.
merge_configs(user, repo, repo_slug) -> MergedConfig — deep-merges dicts, replaces lists, drops repo-file operator-scoped keys with warnings.
classify_persist(entry: str) -> Literal['system', 'repo'] — leading-slash classifier.
resolve_watch_files(build_commands: dict, repo_path: Path) -> list[str] — manifest catalog inference.
resolve_checks(repo_path: Path) -> list[dict] — Makefile/package.json scan.
Hard error on legacy keys (persist_dirs / persist_system_dirs) per decision-4.

components.name: config/repo_config.py (modify — keep public API, swap inner loader)
responsibilities: _load_config() now calls shared.egg_config.repos.load_user_file() and merges with auto-discovered repo file when invoked against a known repo.
get_repo_build_commands() returns merged build_commands and reflects derived watch_files / classified persist (synthesizes legacy persist_dirs + persist_system_dirs fields for the manifest writer).
get_repo_checks() returns derived checks if explicit not set.
Public function signatures unchanged — every existing caller inherits the merged view without code changes.
Hard error path for legacy persist_dirs / persist_system_dirs keys (mention the migration doc).
components.behavior_change: Existing call sites get merged config. Operator-scoped getters (get_writable_repos etc.) remain user-only-sourced.

components.name: sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py (modify — re-route through C1)
responsibilities: _copy_repo_watch_files() reads merged config via shared.egg_config.repos (instead of yaml.safe_load directly).
Manifest write retains existing schema (persist_dirs + persist_system_dirs lists, watch_files list, commands list, extra_packages dict) — produced from the unified persist: by C1's classifier.
No change to docker-setup.py — the build-time consumer keeps reading the same manifest.json shape and the #2090 fail-loud invariants.
components.rationale: Keeping the host→build manifest contract unchanged isolates the schema change from the in-image runtime; only the host writer learns the new shape.

components.name: shared/egg_config/repo_validator.py (new module — write-time validator core)
responsibilities: validate_repo_config(user_cfg, repo_cfg, repo_path) -> ValidationReport — emits errors and warnings as typed records.
Schema validity: required keys, type checks, version range, malformed YAML structure.
Legacy keys: hard-error on persist_dirs / persist_system_dirs / explicit watch_files at top of new schema.
Persistence coherence: build_commands install to /usr/local/bin etc. but persist: omits the parent dir (the #2065 trap).
Persist-vs-build-context coherence: detect 'uv sync' / 'pip install -e .' / 'npm install' patterns and warn when watch_files lacks the source files those need (the #2087 trap).
Makefile target existence: scan target Makefile for each checks.command and error on missing target.
Manifest/watch coherence: install-tool keywords without matching manifest in watch list → warning.
auth_mode: user without GITHUB_USER_TOKEN configured → warning.
persist of empty directory → warning.
curl/wget in build_commands while operator is in private network mode → warning.
local_repos.paths entries must exist on disk → error.
writable_repos entries with no corresponding repo_settings → info.
checkpoint_repo well-formedness (owner/repo) and best-effort accessibility (gh api repos/<...>) → warning.
Repo file containing operator-scoped keys → warning.
Two-tier output (decision-11): errors block, warnings advise.

components.name: egg validate-config CLI subcommand (new — bin/egg or scripts/)
responsibilities: Surface egg validate-config [<repo-path>]; dispatches to C4 and renders a stdout report (errors red, warnings yellow, info green) compatible with scripts/validate-config.py's existing ✓/✗/⚠ format.
Exit code 0 on no errors; nonzero on any error (warnings do not fail).

Reuses scripts/validate-config.py output framing where compatible (decision-6 leans toward extending the existing surface; we add a new subcommand inside that script or as a new script that imports its formatter).

components.name: mcp__egg__validate_repo_config MCP tool (new — orchestrator/mcp_tools.py)
responsibilities: Distinct from the existing mcp__egg__validate_config tool (which validates pipeline configs). The naming collision noted in the refine analysis is resolved by adopting a separate tool name.
Input schema: { repo_path?: string, user_path?: string }; output: ValidationReport JSON.
Used by /onboard-repo skill before write, and by reviewers in BRC if needed.

components.name: skills/onboard-repo/SKILL.md (new)
responsibilities: /onboard-repo <path> entry point. Mirrors skills/egg-setup/SKILL.md style (single SKILL.md, AskUserQuestion-driven).
Phase 1 — detection: inspect repo path; identify lockfiles/manifests; classify by language ladder Python (uv → pip), Node (pnpm → npm → yarn), Go.

Phase 2 — propose build_commands per detection rule (Python uv: install uv to /usr/local/bin + make sandbox-deps + persist [.venv, /usr/local/bin]; Python pip: pip install -r + persist [.venv]; Node: corepack/pnpm/npm install + persist [node_modules]; Go: install Go to /usr/local/go + go mod download + persist [/usr/local/go]; mixed: union).
Phase 3 — propose checks: scan Makefile + package.json scripts; surface what was found.
Phase 4 — AskUserQuestion confirmation for EACH detected build_command (per feedback Q6: always require human confirmation; no auto-write).
Phase 5 — write to <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml; if write blocked, print YAML to stdout and offer to append the per-repo block to ~/.config/egg/repositories.yaml under repo_settings (decision-8).
Phase 6 — call C6 (mcp__egg__validate_repo_config) on the produced file; surface errors and warnings; refuse to commit until errors are resolved.
Detector plug-in seam (per feedback Q7): a registry pattern — register_detector(name, predicate, builder) — so bazel/gradle/multi-stage variants can be added without rewriting the core skill.

responsibilities: JSON Schema for both files — single schema with schemaVersion: 1, two top-level shapes (user vs repo) discriminated by allowed keys.

Example file rewritten to the new schema: unified persist:, derived-by-default checks/watch_files, version: 1, template: (commented placeholder), per-repo blocks both inline (user file) and standalone (repo file).
depended_on_by: humans, validator (loaded as JSON Schema sanity check)

data_flow.host_runtime_load: config.repo_config.get_repo_build_commands(repo) → shared.egg_config.repos.load_merged(repo_slug=repo) → user file (~/.config/egg/repositories.yaml) loaded once + cached → if local_repos.paths or invocation cwd identifies a checkout, repo file (<repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml) loaded → merge_configs() → returned as merged dict → per-getter slicing.
data_flow.host_build_write: sandbox.egg_lib.docker._copy_repo_watch_files() → load_merged() → write /tmp/repo-deps/manifest.json with legacy two-list persist shape produced by classifier → docker-setup.py reads manifest unchanged.
data_flow.validator_invoked: egg validate-config <repo> → C5 → C4.validate_repo_config(load_user_file(), load_repo_file(<repo>), <repo>) → ValidationReport → stdout/stderr render + exit code.
data_flow.onboard_skill: /onboard-repo <path> → C7 detection → AskUserQuestion confirmation → write <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml → mcp__egg__validate_repo_config → if errors: prompt for fix; if warnings: surface; else commit.

alternatives_considered.name: Inline merge inside config/repo_config.py without a shared module
alternatives_considered.description: Keep the merge logic in config/repo_config.py::_load_config() and have sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py import from config/.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: decision-5 explicitly prefers shared/egg_config/repos.py because sandbox/egg_lib does not currently import from config/, which crosses the runtime boundary. Making sandbox depend on config/ would invert today's dependency direction.

alternatives_considered.name: New top-level package egg_repo_config/
alternatives_considered.description: Brand-new package separate from both shared/ and config/.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: decision-5 ruled this out (option opt-3); shared/egg_config/ already houses the validators and constants both runtimes use, so adding a sibling module there is the smallest surface.

alternatives_considered.name: Sequenced PRs (decision-2 opt-1)
alternatives_considered.description: Land schema+validator first, then layered loader, then skill in separate PRs.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Human chose decision-2 opt-2 (one coordinated feature). Sequencing would have made each PR smaller but created in-flight schema churn for two-three releases. The trade-off was discussed in the refine phase and resolved.

alternatives_considered.name: Soft deprecation with warnings
alternatives_considered.description: Accept legacy persist_dirs/persist_system_dirs/explicit watch_files with a deprecation warning indefinitely.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: decision-4 selected hard deprecation. Cleanest schema; prevents legacy-vs-new dual code paths from accumulating; users hand-update per Q1.

alternatives_considered.name: Append-merge as default for lists
alternatives_considered.description: Make checks/persist/watch_files lists union user + repo entries by default.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: decision-9 selected replace by default. Append surprises users when they want an override; simpler to teach replace + (future) extends opt-in.

alternatives_considered.name: Operator-must-opt-in for repo defaults
alternatives_considered.description: Loader reads <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml only when the operator explicitly lists the repo or sets use_repo_defaults: true.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: decision-10 selected silent auto-discovery. Onboarding a new repo with a committed .egg/repositories.yaml should Just Work — opt-in friction defeats the zero-config win.

alternatives_considered.name: Auto-write skill (no per-detection AskUserQuestion)
alternatives_considered.description: Skill writes its inferred config without confirmation when only one lockfile is found.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: feedback Q6 explicitly said always require AskUserQuestion confirmation. Heuristic detection has to fail loudly, not silently bake in a wrong block.

alternatives_considered.name: Single big mcp__egg__validate_config tool serving both pipeline + repo configs
alternatives_considered.description: Reuse the existing tool name with an input discriminator.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Naming collision noted in the refine analysis — existing tool validates PipelineConfig with a different schema. Cleaner to add mcp__egg__validate_repo_config; existing tool's schema and consumers stay stable.

constraints_and_invariants: Backward compatibility on the in-image manifest.json shape: docker-setup.py keeps reading the legacy persist_dirs + persist_system_dirs fields; the schema change is host-side only. This preserves #2090's fail-loud invariants without changes to in-container code.
Operator-scoped keys NEVER leak into a committed repo file; validator emits a warning if they do; loader strips them with a warning at merge time. (Both correctness and leak-hazard considerations.)
Centralized merge: ONE place (shared/egg_config/repos.py) owns the merge rules. Every existing caller inherits the merged view without changes. This is non-negotiable per decision-5.

Hard cutover on legacy keys: loading persist_dirs / persist_system_dirs / explicit watch_files in the NEW schema raises with a clear error pointing to docs/reference/repo-config-schema.md. Existing files at version: (none) are rejected with the same migration pointer (per decision-4).
Two-tier validation: errors block, warnings advise (decision-11). Loader emits warnings via the standard Python logger; CLI/MCP tool surface them in their reports.
Schema versioning from day one (decision-13): version: 1 on both files. Loader gracefully degrades on version > 1.
Detector plug-in seam: register_detector(name, predicate, builder) is exposed so bazel/gradle/multi-stage repos can be slotted in without rewriting the core skill (per feedback Q7).
Heuristic detection has confirmation: every detected build_command in the onboard skill goes through AskUserQuestion (per feedback Q6).
egg's own .egg/repositories.yaml ships in the same change as the loader (per feedback Q2). It is the canonical first-consumer reference.
List merge: replace by default; no extends: keyword (decision-9). All list-valued fields (checks, persist, watch_files, extra_packages.*, local_repos.paths) follow the same rule.
template: field reserved (feedback Q4). Validator allows it; loader stores it; v1 takes no action.

open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.question: How should the onboarding skill detect Makefile lint/test targets when the Makefile uses include directives or recipe variables (e.g. include scripts/*.mk, $(MAKE) -C subdir)?
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.context: feedback Q7 acknowledges unknown variation. The validator's missing-target check needs the same Makefile parser.
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.recommendation: Use a tolerant scan: grep '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:' for direct targets; for include directives, recursively follow at most 2 levels and union the targets; otherwise warn that detection may be incomplete and ask the user to pin checks: explicitly. Defer fully-correct GNU Make parsing to a follow-up.

open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.question: Should the validator's checkpoint_repo accessibility check (gh api repos/<owner/repo>) run by default or only on --strict?
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.context: Network calls in a validator add latency and can fail in private mode where the gh CLI is restricted (decision-11 names this case).
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.recommendation: Best-effort with timeout; skip silently in private network mode (detected via existing private-mode env var). Surface result as a warning, never an error.

open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.question: What is the expected size of the ValidationReport on a complex repo, and should the MCP tool stream or return whole?
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.context: Decision-11 lists 13+ check classes. A monorepo could trigger many warnings.
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.recommendation: Return whole; cap per-class warnings at 20 with an overflow indicator. Consistent with existing scripts/validate-config.py output cap.

open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.question: When auto-discovery finds a <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml that is malformed YAML, do we hard-fail the load (operator can't run egg) or soft-fail with a warning and proceed using only the user file?
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.context: decision-10 says silent skip if absent. Malformed is not absent.
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.recommendation: Hard-error. Silent-skip is for 'file not present'; a malformed file is a deployment bug the operator should see immediately. Surface the parse error and the file path. Document this distinction in docs/reference/repo-config-schema.md.

open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.question: Should the unified persist: list disallow .. components even when leading-slash is absent, or only validate after path resolution?
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.context: Repo-relative paths could escape the repo root via ../something.
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.recommendation: Validator-level error pre-resolution: any entry containing .. components is rejected with a clear message. Stricter than docker-setup.py's runtime denial; we want this caught at config-write time.

open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.question: Naming: mcp__egg__validate_repo_config vs renaming the existing mcp__egg__validate_config to validate_pipeline_config?
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.context: decision-6 chose 'extend the existing tool' but flagged the collision. The existing tool's name is a public surface.
open_questions_for_planner_and_risk_anal.recommendation: Add mcp__egg__validate_repo_config and leave the existing mcp__egg__validate_config alone (validating pipeline config). Renaming the existing tool would break callers; the goal in decision-6 was 'cover humans and agents in one change,' not 'one tool.' We satisfy that with CLI + new MCP tool.

risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.risk: Centralized loader change risks fan-out regressions across ~15 callers
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Public API of config/repo_config.py is preserved. Behavior change is limited to merged-view handling. Test matrix: every public getter has a test that pins both user-only and merged behavior.

risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.risk: Hard deprecation breaks existing operator configs at upgrade time
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Per decision-4 / Q1 hard cutover is accepted. Surface a clear error message linking to docs/reference/repo-config-schema.md. Update CHANGELOG and onboarding docs in the same PR.

risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.risk: Skill heuristic produces a wrong build_command and bakes it into a committed repo file
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: AskUserQuestion confirmation per detected build_command (Q6). Validator runs before commit (C7 phase 6). Detector plug-in seam (Q7) lets us iterate without churning the schema.

risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.risk: Auto-discovery accidentally trusts a hostile <repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml in a cloned repo
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Per-repo file can ONLY set repo-scoped keys (validator strips operator-scoped with warnings). Build_commands run only inside the sandbox build at image-build time; existing /proc /sys /dev path denials remain. Document the trust model: operator opts in by checking out a repo into local_repos.paths.

risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.risk: Persist classifier diverges from docker-setup.py's interpretation
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Classifier is a one-line rule (leading-slash). Tests assert the produced manifest exactly matches what the legacy schema would have produced for equivalent inputs; round-trip property tests.
version: 1 today, LOADER_MAX_SUPPORTED constant gating future bumps; require a docs/reference entry on every bump.

risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.risk: Validator false positives erode user trust
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Two-tier (errors vs warnings) per decision-11. Heuristic checks (manifest/install-tool mismatch, package.json scripts collision) are warnings, never errors. Provide an --ignore <check-name> flag in C5 (CLI) to suppress specific warnings.

risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.risk: Migration of egg's own .egg/repositories.yaml (C9) breaks the egg pipeline mid-rollout
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Land C1+C2+C3+C8 first as separate commits; verify egg pipeline still loads from the user file alone; THEN add C9 in a follow-up commit; keep config/repositories.yaml.example up-to-date as a fallback. Integration tests run end-to-end before merge.

risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.risk: Watch_files derivation misses a manifest the build_commands use
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Validator's install-tool-keyword heuristic (C4) catches the common cases. Manifest catalog v1 is conservative; users override explicitly when wrong. Docker layer caching invariants stay the same as today.

implementation_workstreams_for_task_plan.summary: Add new tool to orchestrator/mcp_tools.py. Schema { repo_path?, user_path? }. Handler dispatches to C4 and serializes ValidationReport.

implementation_workstreams_for_task_plan.summary: Lift the egg per-repo block out of config/repositories.yaml.example into <egg-repo>/.egg/repositories.yaml using the new schema. Verify the egg SDLC pipeline still runs end-to-end.

WS6 + WS7 (CLI + MCP tool) — parallel, both depend on WS5.
